sections.heading: 1. Executive decision and simulation boundary
sections.body: Prepared locally on 27 September 2026 as an advance simulation of 1–15 October 2026. User authorized invented assumptions. Atlas, Company Assistant, coordinated local skills delegated to qualified roster colleagues. Select CNY 50,000 pilot; defer CNY 120,000 full launch. Actual achievements are local artifact generation, calculations and register records. Guest attendance, revenue, costs, satisfaction and launch success are fictional assumptions, not real-world evidence. No external accounts, contacts, payments, bookings, advertisements or travel reservations were used. An unsent text email draft exists only within the management-handoff result.

sections.heading: 2. Options and commercial assumptions
sections.body: Both approaches start with 30 guests at CNY 2,000 each, modeled revenue CNY 60,000. Pilot: budget CNY 50,000, impact 4/5, risk 2/5, score 73.5; planned pre-tax operating profit CNY 10,000. Full: budget CNY 120,000, impact 5/5, risk 4/5, score 52.0; planned operating loss CNY 60,000. Weight inputs impact/risk/cost = 4/3/3. Ratings are invented judgments. Cost envelopes include guest service costs and contingency; do not add them twice. Planned pilot fixed/reserve cost 26,000 and variable cost 800/guest imply break-even ceil(26000/1200)=22 guests. Full fixed/reserve cost 96,000 implies 80 guests, above the initial 30-guest cap. Costs exclude flights, lodging, personal purchases, tax, financing and unrelated corporate overhead; no supplier prices researched or represented as market facts.

sections.heading: 3. Product and campaign
sections.body: Fictional premium one-day Chengdu-inspired experience, three supervised groups of ten. 09:30 welcome/dietary briefing; 10:00 food walk; 11:30 cooking workshop and lunch; 13:30 tea preparation/tasting; 15:30 close. All venues, hosts and availability invented. Includes activities, food, tea and local transfers. Campaign planned 6–10 October: content CNY 3,000, partner mockups CNY 3,000, referral copy CNY 2,000; assumed qualified inquiries 150/90/60, deduplicated total 300. Target 30 guests, conversion 10%, campaign cost per guest at most CNY 266.67. No publication, purchase or outreach.

sections.heading: 4. Business schedule and critical dependencies
sections.body: Calendar-day schedule generated by project-plan: evaluate 1–2 October; design 3–5 October; campaign 6–10 October; tabletop rehearsal 6–7 October in parallel; readiness gate 11 October depends on campaign AND rehearsal; fictional departure 12 October; reconciliation 13–14 October; executive report and knowledge 15 October. Tool finish dates are exclusive, so final finish is 16 October 2026, not an extra workday. Critical chain evaluate > design > campaign > gate > departure > reconcile > report is 15 calendar days. Rehearsal branch has 3 days slack. Dates describe scenario work, not activities actually performed in October.

sections.heading: 5. Qualified staff, capacity and RACI

sections.heading: 7. Readiness and risks
sections.body: Completed checklist: 10 checks, 8 met within tabletop scope, zero gaps, 2 real-world unknown. Unknowns are actual supplier/service verification and applicable legal/tax/licensing/insurance/privacy validation. These block a REAL launch, not completion of this simulation. Eight risk scores (assumed likelihood x impact): food safety 15; real compliance uncertainty 15; venue capacity 12; demand 12; simulation mistaken for evidence 10; overrun 9; weather/access 9; capacity mismatch 8. Mitigations: dietary screening/opt-out and escalation; three groups of ten; fictional indoor/access alternative; 22-guest planned break-even gate; CNY 50,000 total ceiling with reserve included; clear labels and separate real verification. No health, safety or legal certification made.

sections.heading: 8. Excel budget and simulated variance — CNY
sections.body: Category: pilot plan / full plan / pilot fictional actual / actual-minus-pilot variance. Guest services: 24,000 / 24,000 / 24,600 / +600 (+2.5%). Product: 6,000 / 24,000 / 5,500 / -500 (-8.33%). Campaign: 8,000 / 36,000 / 7,500 / -500 (-6.25%). Operations: 7,000 / 24,000 / 6,900 / -100 (-1.43%). Reserve/fallback spend: 5,000 / 12,000 / 2,500 / -2,500 (-50%). TOTAL: 50,000 / 120,000 / 47,000 / -3,000 (-6%). Positive cost variance means overspend. Revenue 60,000 less simulated expense 47,000 = operating profit 13,000; margin 21.67%. CNY 2,500 unused reserve is not expense; no real payments occurred. Labor allocations are included in modeled overhead, not added again. Excel contains editable static numeric values, not live formulas.

sections.heading: 9. Finance forecast and sensitivity
sections.body: Completed finance-forecast uses 30 opening fictional customers, zero additions/churn, 30 average customers monthly. This scenario assumes the SAME 30 guests buy one separately priced themed experience each month; 90 guest-visits, not 90 unique customers. October: revenue 60,000, variable cost 24,600 (820 each), fixed cost 22,400, expense 47,000, operating profit 13,000. November and December each: revenue 60,000, variable 24,000 (800 each), fixed 12,000 (campaign 6,000 + operations 6,000), expense 36,000, profit 24,000. Totals: revenue 180,000, expense 119,000, profit 61,000. October reconciles exactly to simulated actuals. Future repeat demand and cost reductions are speculative and not approved operations, subscriptions, booked revenue or cash. No-repeat case, with future departures and costs avoided, yields October-only profit 13,000. Pilot planned demand sensitivity at 20 guests: 40,000 revenue -16,000 variable -26,000 fixed/reserve = -2,000; at 22 guests profit 400; at 30 guests profit 10,000.

sections.heading: 10. Simulated launch outcome and decision record
sections.body: Advance fictional outcome dated 12 October, review 15 October: assume 300 qualified inquiries, 30 commitments and attendees, no cancellations; conversion 10%. Revenue 60,000, cost 47,000, operating profit 13,000; campaign cost per guest 7,500/30 = 250. Invented survey: 24 responses out of 30 (80%); 14 five-star and 10 four-star responses = 110/24 = 4.5833/5, above 4.5 target. Zero assumed incidents. These figures were invented, not observed or collected. Simulated outcome passes targets, but full launch remains deferred until genuine demand, supply and compliance validation in a separately authorized real project. **Atlas, Company Assistant:** The local workflow is complete: **20 successful skill runs, 16 distinct skills, 7 delegated colleagues and 10 generated files**. No failed or pending runs.

All business outcomes below are fictional assumptions. **Nobody was contacted; no external accounts, payments, bookings or real launch were involved.**

### Executive decision and simulated results

**Selected: CNY 50,000 pilot.** The CNY 120,000 full launch remains deferred.

| Comparison | Pilot | Full launch |
|---|---:|---:|
| Initial guests | 30 | 30 |
| Assumed revenue | CNY 60,000 | CNY 60,000 |
| Budget | CNY 50,000 | CNY 120,000 |
| Planned operating result | **CNY 10,000 profit** | **CNY 60,000 loss** |
| Weighted option score | **73.5** | 52.0 |

The fictional product is a one-day food walk, cooking workshop, lunch and tea experience at **CNY 2,000 per guest**. Scoring used impact/risk/cost weights of **4/3/3**.

**Recorded simulated pilot outcome:**
- Spending: **CNY 47,000**, or **CNY 3,000 under budget (6%)**
- Revenue: **CNY 60,000**
- Pre-tax operating profit: **CNY 13,000**, margin **21.67%**
- Assumed attendance: **30 guests**
- Assumed satisfaction: **4.58/5 from 24 fictional responses**
- Assumed incidents: **zero**

These are modeled results—not collected sales, survey or safety evidence.

Also created: a Word decision brief, Excel dependency schedule, Excel RACI, campaign brief and launch checklist.

### Delegated staff and capacity

All delegated skills matched the colleagues’ assigned skills. Hours are **assumed preparation effort / configured free capacity**, not calendar reservations.

| Colleague and role | Hours | Executed steps |
|---|---:|---|
| Chen — Director | 3 / 9 | S03, S13: approach and outcome decisions |
| Wang — Sales lead | 6 / 22 | S02, S17: proposal and management handoff |
| Zhao — Product lead | 8 / 21 | S06, S09, S18: campaign and milestone tracking |
| He — Operations lead | 9 / 22 | S01, S04, S05, S07, S14, S20: capacity, schedule, RACI, risks and tracking |

| Deng — Finance lead | 8 / 20 | S10–S12, S19: variance, budget, forecast and PDF |

| **Total** | **40 / 142** | **20 completed calls** |

### Executed plan and dependencies

The published plan and PDF contain the full call-level dependency map:

1. **S01–S03:** Capacity → option comparison → simulated decision.
2. **S04–S08:** Schedule → responsibilities and campaign → risks → readiness checklist.
3. **S09–S12:** Preparation milestone → simulated variance → budget and forecast.
4. **S13–S16:** Outcome decision → outcome milestone → knowledge saved → retrieval verified.
5. **S17–S20:** Word handoff → handoff milestone → PDF → final closure record.

**Scenario dates:** preparation starts **1 October 2026**; campaign **6–10 October**; readiness gate **11 October**; fictional departure **12 October**; reconciliation **13–14 October**; reporting **15 October**. These future events were simulated in advance on **27 September 2026**.

### Forecast, controls and reuse

- **October–December conditional forecast:** CNY **180,000 revenue**, **119,000 expense**, **61,000 operating profit**. This assumes the same 30 fictional guests return monthly—**90 visits, not 90 acquired customers**. Without repeats, and avoiding subsequent costs, the October-only result remains CNY 13,000.
- **Eight risks assessed.** Checklist: **8 tabletop requirements met, 2 real-world requirements unknown**. Supplier verification and compliance remain unresolved; no real launch clearance is implied.
- **Seven local records saved:** two decisions, four tracking milestones and one knowledge note.
- Knowledge query **`CHENGDU-FOOD-TEA-202610`** successfully retrieved the saved playbook with provenance.

Open **Files** for all artifacts and **Activity** for exact call inputs, outputs and completed statuses. No further skill operation or approval is needed to finish this simulation.
